units.reason: After standard smooth FIO geometry and cited analytic microlocal/semiclassical tools, the author constructs a homogeneous analytic operator calculus that preserves analytic function-space regularity: factorial-controlled formal amplitudes and their Borel realizations, complex contour/stationary-phase estimates, and coordinate/phase changes must give analytic-regularizing errors rather than merely exponentially small errors in fixed smooth norms. These estimates are used to define operators consistently across real-analytic cone-bundle charts and prove the actual stationary-phase reduction/composition properties in Theorem4.10. This is one nonroutine H3 analytic-calculus proof core beyond applying smooth FIO composition or treating analytic remainders as smooth ones; the many amplitude/phase helper propositions are supporting parts, not independent extra problems.

With the general analytic FIO calculus available, the Szego result still needs a new CR-specific proof: quantize the classical contact normal form, solve the all-orders subprincipal conjugation through factorial-controlled analytic-symbol transport/commutator estimates, realize it on FBI-local function spaces, and glue the self-adjoint rank-one parametrix. The original seven-step argument then identifies the true L2 projector with that parametrix modulo an operator from analytic functionals to analytic functions, using local model hypoellipticity, duality and error-square identities. These analytic normal-form and actual-projector remainder mechanisms give a distinct H3 theorem beyond the general FIO calculus. Toeplitz algebra, analytic hypoellipticity and propagator applications remain supporting/consequence material without extra count.

distinctness: General analytic operator definition/stationary-phase/composition versus additional CR analytic transport normal form and true Szego projector analytic-remainder identification; distinct conclusions with shared calculus, not alternate proofs or formats of the same result.
